title: Microsoft Edge: opt-in for launching Edge when Windows starts on managed devices
summary: Hold: the Group Policy route starts inside Administrative Templates without explaining how to reach that node. The registry details, user-choice behaviour and reported rollout dates are supported by Microsoft documentation and the roadmap record.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: Microsoft plans an opt-in experience for users on managed devices to choose whether Edge launches when Windows starts.
claims.quote: Microsoft Edge will introduce an opt-in experience that allows users on managed devices to choose whether Edge launches automatically when Windows starts.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: The roadmap names LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled with opt-in, opt-out and user-choice configurations.
claims.quote: Administrators can also manage this behavior through the LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled policy with opt-in, opt-out, and user-choice configurations.

claims.claim: The unconfigured experience is user-opt-in, with users choosing whether to enable automatic launch.
claims.quote: If you don't configure this policy, Microsoft Edge won't launch automatically when Windows starts by default. Users are periodically shown an opt-in banner to turn it on, and can enable or disable automatic launch anytime from settings.

claims.claim: The policy page says periodically without publishing the banner's frequency.
claims.quote: Searched: LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled opt-in banner periodically frequency rollout date. Opened the policy and Stable release notes; read returned Beta and archived Stable excerpts. The policy page gives 'periodically' and no interval.
